chunks: From him, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him about the testimony of the mukatab (a slave who has contracted for his manumission), how should one rule regarding it? He said: 'His testimony is valid to the extent of what has been freed from him, if it was not stipulated for him that if he becomes unable [to pay], we will return him [to slavery]. But if it was stipulated for him that [we will return him], his testimony is not valid until he pays or it is established that he has become unable [to pay].'

He said, so I said: 'How is the calculation of that?' He said: 'If he has paid half or one-third, and he testifies for you for two thousand against a man, you are given from your right what was freed of the two thousand [i.e., the proportion corresponding to the fraction paid].'
ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a mukatab's testimony in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the nuanced fiqh of a mukatab’s testimony, linking its validity to his financial status and the specific terms of his manumission contract (*kitabah*). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on conditional stipulations (*shurut*), where the master’s right to reclaim slavery upon default suspends the mukatab’s legal capacity until full payment or proven insolvency is established. The example provided illustrates the proportional adjustment of witness value, reflecting the practical application of justice in commercial transactions.
